It’s hard to explain when all this really started. I just know that lately—maybe the last few months?—I feel like I can’t settle. Even in curatorial meetings, I’m up and down from my chair, wandering to look at a slide or a catalog file, then realizing everyone else stayed seated. My legs feel like they’re buzzing. When I’m in the galleries, I’ll pace instead of just standing with the group. 

People at work have started pointing out that I cut them off mid-sentence. I’ll jump in with an idea about a display or conservation issue before they’ve finished talking. I don’t mean to, it’s like the words just come out. I’m constantly darting from one task to another—condition reports, emails, loan agreements—but I lose the thread and forget what I was doing. Planning an exhibition feels overwhelming; I start organizing the checklist, then get sidetracked by some tiny detail and never finish.

What’s frightening me are these odd moments when I’m alone in a gallery and I’m almost sure I hear someone whisper my name, or see movement in the corner of my eye when no one is there. I question myself—is it just the acoustics, the lighting? But it leaves me unsettled and more keyed up, like I’m always on edge.
D003-D005_h021.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D003-D005_h021.answer: A & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D003-D005_h022.question:
I’m not really sure when all this started; it feels like it’s been building over the past few months, maybe longer, but it’s hard to pin down. At work in the studio, I can’t sit still. I’ll be in the middle of a mix review and suddenly I’m up, pacing around the room, fiddling with cables or checking mics for no real reason, even when the client’s talking. My legs are always bouncing, like I’ve got this motor running inside me that I can’t shut off.

People tell me I cut them off a lot. In sessions, I’ll jump in over musicians or the producer before they finish, or I’ll tweak something on the board without asking. I notice I drift during long takes or meetings—my focus just slides away—and then I lose track of what we decided. My sessions end up messy: files mislabeled, projects half-finished because I got pulled into something else.

Lately I’ve also been hearing faint sounds—like someone calling my name or music playing in the hallway—when nobody else seems to notice anything. It throws me off and makes it even harder to stay organized or keep my mind on what I’m supposed to be doing.
D003-D005_h022.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D003-D005_h022.answer: A & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D003-D005_h023.question:
I guess the main thing is I just can’t seem to sit still or stay with one thing. Even right now, I kind of want to get up and walk around. That happens a lot in meetings or when I’m on calls with clients—I’ll suddenly stand up, pace, fiddle with stuff on my desk, and it’s hard to just stay in my chair. My coworkers joke that I’m “always on fast‑forward,” because I’m constantly moving, bouncing my leg, tapping, or getting up to “check something” every few minutes.

I tend to cut people off mid-sentence without meaning to. In stand‑ups, I’ll jump in over others or answer questions that weren’t really directed at me. It’s like my mouth goes before my brain. When I’m coding, I drift off, open random tabs, start a new feature before finishing the old one—my attention just slides away. My tasks get messy, half-finished branches everywhere, missed tickets because I lose track of what I was supposed to prioritize.

Over the past several months, on top of all that, I’ve had moments where I’m not sure if what I’m hearing or sensing is actually there—like faint voices or whispers when I’m alone, or feeling like someone is behind me when I know the apartment’s empty. It makes it even harder to concentrate, and I can’t tell if this is all one problem or a few different things going on.
D003-D005_h023.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D003-D005_h023.answer: A & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D003-D005_h024.question:
It’s hard to put into words, but over the last few years I just can’t seem to sit still. Even when I’m at the front counter, I keep popping back into the kitchen, then out again, like I can’t stay in one place. If I try to sit and do the books, I’m up and down from the chair, pacing around the bakery for no good reason. I feel like I’ve got this motor running inside me.

My staff tell me I cut them off a lot. Customers will be talking and I jump in before they’re finished, or I step into conversations in the back without thinking. I don’t mean to be rude; it’s like my mouth moves before my brain.

I’m having a harder time focusing, too. I’ll start placing an order and find myself staring at the screen or drifting off, then realize I’ve missed half of what the supplier just said. The invoices and schedules end up in messy piles, and I lose track of what’s been done.

On top of that, sometimes I’m convinced I hear someone say my name or whisper in the shop when no one’s there, or I get these odd, uneasy feelings that someone’s watching me, even though I know that doesn’t really make sense.

A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bulimia Nervosa

    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D003-D005_h024.answer: A & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D003-D005_h025.question:
I’m not really sure where to start. For maybe… a year? Maybe longer?… I just can’t seem to stay still. Even sitting here, my leg keeps bouncing, and in surveillance jobs I keep catching myself pacing or wandering off when I’m supposed to stay put and watch a door. It feels like there’s a motor running inside me. I’ll stand up in meetings with clients without really thinking, or drift around the room when everyone else is seated.

I also cut people off a lot—clients, cops, even my ex—jumping in before they finish. It’s like I’m afraid I’ll lose the thought if I wait. On cases, I start tasks and then my mind drifts; I’ll be reviewing footage and suddenly realize I’ve been staring at the same frame, thinking about something else entirely. My office is a mess—files from different cases mixed together, notes on napkins. I try to organize it, but I get overwhelmed and move on to something else.

Lately, there are moments when I’m not sure if what I’m noticing—shadows, whispers, someone watching me—is just me being jumpy from the job or something my mind is adding. That’s part of what’s really starting to worry me.

A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
